To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the external concentration of calcium ion is an important regulator of stem cell proliferation, and of differentiation to larval and non-larval cell types; 2) the external concentration is the key determinant of stem cell fate; 3) the internal concentration of calcium ion may also play a role in stem cell differentiation.

1) stem cells from mid-gut tissue of the insect Heliothis vierscens can proliferate and differentiate in cell culture; 2) proliferation and differentiation of these stem cells is altered by changes in the concentration of external Ca(2+) (Ca(2+)(out)); 3) the effect of Ca(2+)(Out) on stem cell proliferation and differentiation depends on the concentration of Ca(Out) and the presence of other ions in the culture medium;

(1) the concentration of calcium ions outside the cells affects the fate of midgut stem cells, and (2) the effect of calcium ions outside cells is to increase proliferation of stem cells and to induce differentiation of stem cells into larval epithelium.

the stem cells from the midgut of the tobacco budworm, Heliothis vierscens, are sensitive to changes in Ca2+ concentration.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the external calcium ion concentration regulates the rate of stem cells proliferation, as well as their differentiation to larval or to non-larval midgut cell types.
stem cells in the midgut of the insect H. virescens can be induced to proliferate and differentiate to larval midguts or to non-mid-gut cell types, by altering external Ca(2+) concentrations.
